title: Automation–distribution coordination break
summary: Automation raises productivity, but wages tie income to jobs. As routine tasks and whole jobs are automated, income falls even as abundance grows (the productivity-wage gap). The institutions that once distributed gains broadly (unions, progressive taxation, minimum wage) are the missing coordination layer.
source: Ch09 §9.2 — 'The technology works. The economy breaks.' and Autor on the productivity-wage gap
